item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem: In which figure are one-half of the dots black?
item.figure_description:
Four square boxes labeled A, B, C, and D, each containing black (filled) and white (open) circles:
- Option A: Contains 4 circles in a 2 by 2 arrangement. Top row: 1 black circle, 1 white circle. Bottom row: 2 white circles.
- Option B: Contains 6 circles in 2 rows of 3. Top row: white, black, white. Bottom row: black, black, white.
- Option C: Contains 3 circles. Top row: white on the left, black on the right. Bottom row: black on the left.
- Option D: Contains 5 circles arranged in an X pattern like the five dots on a die. Top-left is black, top-right is white, center is white, bottom-left is white, and bottom-right is black.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.figure_description:
Five identical squares, labeled A through E, each partitioned and shaded differently:
- Option A: The square is divided horizontally into 5 equal strips. The top 2 strips are shaded grey and the bottom 3 strips are unshaded (white).
- Option B: The square is divided by a diagonal from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner, and a line segment from the center to the bottom-right corner. The entire upper-left triangular half is shaded grey, the right triangular section is shaded grey, and the bottom triangular section is unshaded.
- Option C: The square is divided by two vertical lines into three strips: a narrow shaded strip on the left, a wide unshaded strip in the middle, and a narrow shaded strip on the right.
- Option D: An unshaded triangle has its base along the entire bottom edge of the square and its apex at the midpoint of the top edge. The two right triangles flanking it on the left and right are shaded grey.
- Option E: The square is divided by two vertical lines into 3 equal-width vertical strips. The left strip and the right strip are shaded grey, and the middle strip is unshaded.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.figure_description:
The stem includes a diagram of a rectangle divided into 2 rows of 3 equal squares (6 squares total). The 4 squares in the first two columns are shaded grey, and the 2 squares in the third column are unshaded (white).

The response options show four diagrams composed of squares:
- Option A: A horizontal row of 3 equal squares, all 3 shaded grey.
- Option B: A horizontal row of 4 equal squares; the first 3 squares are unshaded and the 4th square is shaded grey.
- Option C: A vertical rectangle divided into 4 rows of 2 equal squares (8 squares total). The top 6 squares (3 rows) are shaded grey, and the bottom 2 squares (1 row) are unshaded.
- Option D: A horizontal row of 6 equal squares; the first 3 squares are shaded grey and the last 3 squares are unshaded.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
